primary_sources.title: Model-Agnostic Online Certificate-Driven Calibration for Time Series Forecasting Under Distribution Shift
primary_sources.authors: Chenfeng Huang; Zixuan Ma; George Michailidis

verified_claims: The paper explicitly proposes a model-agnostic online martingale PAC-Bayes framework with finite-sample certificates under temporal dependence and distribution shift; its concentration adapts to loss scale and predictable variation.
The paper uses the certificate as a surrogate regularizer for online calibration on top of a fixed forecasting backbone.
The corrective component is a gated residual Bayesian head; when its gate is closed, prediction reverts to the fixed backbone.
The protocol is predict-then-update: target outcomes become available only after forecasting and affect later predictions.
The official author repository exists and describes itself as the UAI 2026 OMPB implementation.
verification.scope_correction: The primary source does NOT establish the cross-field worker's proposed future controller as a theorem-equivalent 'certificate gate' that authorizes or rejects each aggressive allocation proposal. In OMPB, the certificate is used as a surrogate regularizer in online calibration, while the residual head has its own learned gate and backbone fallback. Therefore the worker's fixed-defensive-backbone plus separately certified corrective-allocation idea is supported only as an architectural/design precedent, not as a directly transferable finite-sample guarantee for allocation variance or one-step safety. The worker already labels this direction as a motif/transfer requiring a separate proxy certificate, which is the source-correct interpretation.
verification.reproduction_boundary: No independent end-to-end OMPB numerical reproduction was performed. The official repository README states that datasets are not bundled and must be downloaded separately, and paper-result reproduction requires manually setting dataset/backbone training epochs. This audit verifies source semantics and implementation provenance, not reported accuracy/stability tables.

adverse_control.question: Can the OMPB result be cited as direct evidence that an anytime confidence sequence over an allocation proxy safely gates an aggressive particle-allocation controller?
adverse_control.answer: No. The cited paper's certified object, model, loss, and calibration architecture differ, and its abstract describes the certificate as a surrogate regularizer rather than a per-action authorization predicate. Any proxy-to-true-allocation bridge remains a separate estimand and must be proved or tested in the target system.
